subject: Energy
title: The Economics of Storage
description: One-minute skill: The Economics of Storage.

hook.text: Storage earns money by buying low and selling high—charging when electricity is cheap and discharging when it's costly.

buildup.text: Arbitrage profits depend on price spreads—the bigger the gap between off-peak and peak prices, the more storage earns.

discovery.text: Storage also earns from grid services—frequency regulation, capacity payments, and congestion relief.

twist.text: Lithium-ion costs fell 90% since 2010—from $1,100/kWh to about $140/kWh, making grid storage economically viable.

climax.text: At $100/kWh, batteries become cheap enough to displace gas peaking plants—analysts expect this threshold soon.

punchline.text: Buy cheap, sell dear—storage profits from price swings.

quiz.question: How do grid-scale batteries primarily earn revenue?
options: Charging cheap and discharging when prices are high
